desc: Establish that G (comparability graph of an interval order) is P5-free, so a minimum-weight simple path is chordless with at most 3 edges (4 vertices); with positive weights the optimum is among lengths 1–3.
Parse N, W, intervals, Q queries with 1-indexed arrays and fast I/O.
Build minL[x] = min W_i with L_i = x and minR[x] = min W_i with R_i = x over coordinates 1..2N.
Build prefR[x] = min_{R_i < x} W_i and suffL[x] = min_{L_i > x} W_i for O(1) length-2 common-neighbor queries.
Build iterative range-min segment trees over minL and minR for the length-3 crossing queries.

Per query: disjoint (R_s < L_t or R_t < L_s) -> W_s+W_t; else length-2 via min(prefR[min(L_s,L_t)], suffL[max(R_s,R_t)]); else for strict crossing (L_s<L_t<=R_s<R_t or symmetric) length-3 via RMQ over L in [R_s+1,R_t] and R in [L_s,L_t-1]; take min else -1.
Output answers line by line (verified against both provided samples).
